title: Anti-fascist march and clashes with far-right group in Gorizia

tea.why: Anti-fascist groups held a demonstration in Gorizia, where tensions rose near the local headquarters of CasaPound and Blocco Studentesco.
tea.want: Protesters demanded the closure of all fascist offices in the region.
tea.changed: Nov 7: Police intervened as far-right group members attempted to break through a blockade, resulting in three injured officers.

summary: An anti-fascist march took place in Gorizia, drawing around 200 participants, including a group from Ravenna. Organised by Collettivo Giovani Antifa, the demonstration proceeded under heavy police presence. Tensions flared near Piazza Municipio and Via Mazzini when members of CasaPound and Blocco Studentesco exchanged insults and provocations with the route and attempted to force past a police blockade. Officers in anti-riot gear intervened to contain the push, resulting in three police officers sustaining injuries, with one suffering a shoulder dislocation requiring twenty-one days of prognosis. Despite the clashes and verbal altercations, the main demonstration eventually resumed its path toward Piazza Vittoria.
demands: The closure of all fascist offices in the region
response: According to the sources, police deployed sixty agents—including about forty reinforcements—who used anti-riot gear, shields, helmets, and batons to contain an attempt by far-right individuals to breach a blockade, resulting in three injured officers.

updates.text: An anti-fascist march organized by Collettivo Giovani Antifa started in Gorizia with approximately 200 participants under heavy rain.
Tensions escalated near Via Mazzini as far-right individuals from CasaPound and Blocco Studentesco attempted to break a police cordon.
Police confirmed that three officers were injured during the containment efforts, with one sustaining a dislocated shoulder.
